# Independent audit: one-cap base-moment correction

**PASS.** Audited Sections 1--8 of
`candidate d77abe6ff171c6f3`.

The finite minimum-removal LP, its attained dual, and the identity
r_*=m_E-T_j follow with the stated signs. The local inactive-capacity
regime is exact because every nonnegative coefficient is bounded by its
total gauge mass. The strict-gain/exposed-face alternative is also exact;
rank zero is separately and correctly handled.

The quoted one-actual-cap moment theorem applies to every nonzero
continuous normal here because q=d. Its realization preserves only total
mass and base moment, exactly as the note states. The complementary CLOSED
cap has no shared positive d-volume boundary. Positive retained fiber
mass supplies a point strictly inside the retained side, and nearby
ambient interior points prove the result is an actual body.

The signed continuous-centroid equation retains both added and removed
moments. The sharper cost r_D is legitimate: removed mass outside the
old D can cancel at most the added mass there, so deleting old mass is
the only negative direct source contribution. The coarea shift cost is
uniform in integer tilt and handles vertical caps separately.

The two rectangle computations, including the removal thresholds,
endpoint-volume equality, centroid (20), and strict rational inequality
(21), check. Their initial slack and above-half-total-mass scope are
explicit; no zero-slack result is inferred.

Section 8's first mixed-volume derivative is strictly positive exactly
at a proper full-dimensional fiber inclusion, by the displayed
Brunn--Minkowski lower bound. The gauge equality then places all such
indices on one proper exposed face at a strict-slack maximum. Its
same-base-centroid corollary uses the full positive volume increments
on that same face and is valid. It concerns only the extraction's
positive base set, as stated.

This is complementary to the exponential inner-erosion correction:
the one-cap correction can attain a boundary-supported minimum-removal
law, whereas the local erosion construction keeps an interior removal
mean and pays slightly more mass to alter every fiber only by a small
parallel offset. Neither supplies an unproved universal active-cap sign.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
